## Android

### External and system entries

| Screen | Entry | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S-AND-060 | widget | Home-screen widget drawn by the launcher outside the app route tree; it is a glanceable surface entered from the device home screen, not a destination inside the app navigation. |
| S-AND-061 | deep_link | Landing opened from a split invitation link shared outside the app; the invitee may not be a user yet (product/08 section 7, P08), so it has no in-app navigation parent. |
| S-AND-062 | deep_link | Landing opened from a household invitation link; no membership exists before acceptance and eligibility cannot be bypassed through an invitation (product/01 section 3.9). |
| S-AND-065 | notification | Landing opened from a notification about one clarification item; it is entered only from that notification, so it has no navigation parent. |

## D19 platform allocation

Parity, divergence or absence per capability and platform, with the registry flows that deliver it. Every divergence records its user/job rationale and a pending CDO approval; none is approved.

| Capability | Name | Journeys | Android | Web | Admin | Rationale | CDO approval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CAP-001 | Sign-in, recovery and app shell | J01, J02, J11 | parity: F-AND-01, F-AND-02 | parity: F-WEB-01 | divergent: F-ADM-01 | Customers sign in, recover access and reach the app shell on Android and web; operators use a separate administrative identity domain with hardware-factor sessions and their own recovery, so the admin entry diverges by design (ADR-020 section 7). | pending |
| CAP-002 | Consent, eligibility and device permissions | J01, J02, J03 | parity: F-AND-03 | divergent: F-WEB-01 | absent | Purpose consent and age eligibility apply on both customer platforms, signed out before registration (ADR-019 section 2; adult-only, failing closed before profile creation, product/01 section 3.9); SMS and notification-access permissions exist only on Android, whose capture depends on them (product/01 section 3.8). Consent is the customer's own decision: operators have no consent destination. | pending |
| CAP-003 | Debt status, strategies and scenarios | J01, J04 | parity: F-AND-04, F-AND-05 | parity: F-WEB-03, F-WEB-04 | absent | Debt tracking and strategy decisions are the customer's own job on Android and web, where desktop web adds dense comparison and side-by-side derivation (product/08 section 8.2); the admin console is powerful over the system, not over user financial data (product/01 section 2.2). | pending |
| CAP-004 | Transactions, accounts, import and export | J03 | parity: F-AND-06 | parity: F-WEB-02 | absent | Account, category and manual transaction management are explicit web work alongside Android (product/01 section 3.8); operators cannot read transaction descriptions or balances by default (product/01 section 2.2). | pending |
| CAP-005 | Capture health, clarification and rules | J03 | parity: F-AND-07 | divergent: F-WEB-05 | absent | Automatic capture depends on Android-only permissions and stays on Android (product/01 section 3.8), so web resolves clarifications and manages rules without a capture-health view; operators never read raw message content (product/01 section 2.2). | pending |
| CAP-006 | Email and receipt capture | J03 | parity: F-AND-08 | absent | absent | Android is capture-first and web analysis-heavy (PenniLogic/docs#74 context); the pinned registry has no web or admin flow for mailbox or receipt capture, and raw message content never reaches operators (product/01 section 2.2). Whether web needs receipt upload is open for the IA review. | pending |
| CAP-007 | Income, budgets, goals and net worth | J05 | parity: F-AND-09, F-AND-10 | parity: F-WEB-06 | absent | Web covers income and budgeting, goals and net worth for parity with Android (product/01 section 3.8); this is the customer's own planning data, which operators cannot browse (product/01 section 2.2). | pending |
| CAP-008 | Multi-currency reporting | J05 | absent | parity: F-WEB-12 | absent | Per-currency overviews and reporting-currency changes serve the power user who compares accounts and currencies on a large screen (product/08 section 7, P05); the pinned registry has no Android or admin flow for them, which the IA review should confirm. | pending |
| CAP-009 | Adaptive failures and debt widget | J01, J05 | parity: F-AND-16 | absent | absent | The home-screen widget and constrained-device recovery are Android platform jobs; narrow web remains a complete management fallback instead of a widget (product/08 section 8.2), and operators have no customer surface. | pending |
| CAP-010 | Split groups and settlement | J06 | parity: F-AND-11 | parity: F-WEB-07 | absent | Splitting is explicit web work alongside Android (product/01 section 3.8); group expenses are user financial data that operators cannot browse (product/01 section 2.2). | pending |
| CAP-011 | Family, household and safe exit | J07 | parity: F-AND-12 | parity: F-WEB-08 | absent | Family features are explicit web work alongside Android (product/01 section 3.8); household data is shared only between users, so no operator destination exists that could reveal it (product/01 section 2.2). | pending |
| CAP-012 | Assistant and provider settings | J08 | parity: F-AND-13 | parity: F-WEB-09 | absent | AI and bring-your-own-key settings are explicit web work alongside Android (product/01 section 3.8); operators configure providers, models, routing and spend caps for the whole system (product/01 section 2.2, CAP-016) and have no destination for a user's assistant history. | pending |
| CAP-013 | Billing, notifications and retention | J09 | parity: F-AND-14 | divergent: F-WEB-10 | absent | Web covers billing, invoices and the cross-channel notification preference centre (product/01 section 3.8); retention milestones and digests have no web screen in the pinned registry. Operators change plans and refunds through their own capabilities, not the customer's billing pages. | pending |
| CAP-014 | Trust, rights and support | J10, J11 | parity: F-AND-15 | parity: F-WEB-11 | divergent: F-ADM-06, F-ADM-07 | Customers raise rights and support requests on Android and web; operators fulfil them from redacted queues with independent approval and immutable audit, never by browsing records (product/08 sections 8.3 and 9.3). | pending |
| CAP-015 | Operator access, lifecycle and production access | J11 | absent | absent | parity: F-ADM-02, F-ADM-03, F-ADM-09 | Unmasking, elevation, operator lifecycle and production access are purpose-built operator flows in the separate admin console and identity domain (product/08 section 8.3, ADR-020 sections 3 and 7); customers have no operator destination. | pending |
| CAP-016 | Plans, AI operations, audit and release evidence | J12 | absent | absent | parity: F-ADM-04, F-ADM-05, F-ADM-08, F-ADM-10 | Plans, feature flags, quotas, AI providers and spend caps, aggregate analytics and audit review are the system powers of the admin console (product/01 section 2.2), and incidents and break-glass are operator destinations (product/08 section 8.3); customers see only their own plan and assistant settings. | pending |
